mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary policy, boosting equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing consumer and business spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant positive correlation with low FEDFUNDS levels (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4% signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings expectations decline over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If 5-day forward returns are positive when UNRATE exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with increasing housing starts indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as consumer and business confidence rises.
failure_condition: Negative 60-day returns despite positive GDPC1 and HOUST growth.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production in a late-cycle expansion may signal overproduction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as growth peaks and margins compress over 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive 20-day returns when INDPRO exceeds 105 in late-cycle.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate increases borrowing costs, reducing investment and consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
High retail and food services sales indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as revenues and earnings grow.
Increasing employment and housing starts indicate economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days as both labor market and housing sector thrive.
failure_condition: Negative 20-day returns despite increases in PAYEMS and HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: High CPI indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
